items.body:
TLDR: The DC-DC workaround introduced in https://github.com/jgromes/RadioLib/pull/1864 triggers ASAN warnings, indicating a buffer overrun. **Describe the bug** `LR2021::setDCDCworkaround()` and `LR2021::resetDCDCworkaround()` pass `sizeof(uint32_t)` as the `len` argument of `readRegMem32()` / `writeRegMem32()`. Both functions count `len` in 32-bit words: `readRegMem32()` reads `len*sizeof(uint32_t)` bytes and fills `data[0..len-1]`, and `writeCommon()` sends `len` words. So each call moves 4 words where 1 is intended. In `src/modules/LR2021/LR2021_cmds_chip_control.cpp` (added in `67d7121d2a`, unchanged on master `bf07c6dd4`): - line 352: `readRegMem32(RADIOLIB_LR2021_REG_DCDC_ADC_CTRL, &adcCtrlRaw, sizeof(adcCtrlRaw))` writes `data[1..3]`, which is 12 bytes of stack past the local `uint32_t adcCtrlRaw`. - lines 374 and 390: `writeRegMem32(RADIOLIB_LR2021_REG_DCDC_FREQ_LF, &freq_lf, sizeof(freq_lf))` reads 12 bytes of stack past the local `uint32_t freq_lf`, and sends them to the three registers after `DCDC_FREQ_LF`. Both functions run from inside the driver: `setDCDCworkaround()` from `setRxPath()`, `resetDCDCworkaround()` from `setPacketType()`. So every LR2021 user reaches them during `begin()` and on `setRxBoostedGainMode()`, on either regulator. The first word is correct, so the workaround itself appears to work, which is why it passes on hardware. Semtech's reference implementation, which these functions port (`lr20xx_workarounds.c` in Lora-net/usp `351b2015`), passes `1` at each of these calls. Found with AddressSanitizer in a host build, using a stub HAL that answers every SPI byte with a CMD_OK status (0x04). cppcheck 2.17.1 with the repo's settings, and GCC 14 with `-Warray-bounds=2 -Wstringop-overflow=4`, don't flag it.

items.title: [LR11x0][LR2021] Reply to a get command is sometimes read before the chip has it ready

labels.name: question
labels.description: Generic question about code or usage

labels.name: stale
labels.description: Issue was left inactive for too long

items.body:
**Describe the bug**

On the LR11x0 and LR2021 families a read command is two SPI transactions: send the
opcode, then read the reply. When the second transaction happens before the chip has
the reply ready, the chip sends its default `[stat 2B][irq 4B]` stream instead, and
`LRxxxx::SPIcommand()` returns those bytes as if they were the reply. The status byte
itself is valid, so `SPIparseStatus()` reports success and the caller has no way to
tell that the payload is not an answer to its command.

The received packet length is where this hurts most.

`LR2021::getRxPktLength()` builds a 16-bit value from the first two payload bytes, so
it returns `irq[31:16]`. With RX_DONE (bit 18) set that is exactly 4. With TX_DONE or
CRC_ERROR also set it becomes 12 or 68 - plausible enough to pass as a real length.

`LR11x0::getRxBufferStatus()` takes the length from `buff[0]` and the buffer offset
from `buff[1]`, so it returns `irq[31:24]` and `irq[23:16]`. All RX-relevant flags of
this family live in the two low bytes, so the length comes back as 0; and if
CMD_ERROR (bit 22) is set, the offset comes back as 0x40, which shifts the payload.

`readData()` then reads that many bytes and clears the Rx buffer, so the packet is
destroyed. Nothing reports an error, because the read itself succeeded.

Measured on an LR2021 at SF7 in a live LoRa mesh: frames of 50 and 133 bytes were
reported as `len=4`. In dense bursts, where several nodes answer at once and the chip
is busy, this hit roughly a third of the frames. A second receiver on the same channel
logged the same frames with correct lengths.

Every other `get` is exposed the same way - `getRSSI()`, `getSNR()`, `getRssiInst()`,
`getVbat()`, `getTemp()` - so a caller can also get a wrong RSSI or SNR without any
indication. `getIrqStatus()` is the one exception, because it IS that default stream;
that is also what makes the mechanism easy to confirm, since the bogus length is
always the top bytes of the IRQ word.

As for why the reply is read early: `Module::SPItransferStream()` does
`delayMicroseconds(1)` after the first transaction and then polls BUSY for a low
level. If BUSY has not risen within that microsecond, the loop exits immediately and
the read follows.

**To Reproduce**

The race itself is timing dependent, but it can be provoked deterministically by doing
what the driver does and skipping the BUSY wait on purpose. Setting the status width to
0 keeps both status bytes visible, the same way `LRxxxx::getIrqStatus()` reads the
default stream:

```c++
// two transactions, BUSY wait deliberately skipped
mod->SPIwriteStream(RADIOLIB_LR2021_CMD_GET_RX_PKT_LENGTH, NULL, 0, false, false);
mod->spiConfig.widths[RADIOLIB_MODULE_SPI_WIDTH_STATUS] = Module::BITS_0;
mod->spiConfig.widths[RADIOLIB_MODULE_SPI_WIDTH_CMD]    = Module::BITS_0;
uint8_t buff[4] = { 0 };
mod->SPIreadStream(RADIOLIB_LRXXXX_CMD_NOP, buff, sizeof(buff), false, false);
// buff[0..1] = status word, buff[2..3] = the reply - or the top half of the IRQ word
```

Measured that way on the bench, eight reads with the wait skipped followed by one
proper read, repeated four times. `cmd` is the command status field of stat1, bits 3:1:

```
nowait  stat=04  cmd=2 (CMD_OK)   val=0    <- top half of the IRQ word, not the length
wait    stat=06  cmd=3 (CMD_DAT)  val=50   <- the real length of the last packet
```

32 out of 32 early reads returned the status stream and every one reported `CMD_OK`;
the properly waited reads reported `CMD_DAT` and the correct length.

The same thing measured in the live receive path is more convincing. Skipping the wait
on every fourth length read, in a working mesh at SF7:

```
first=4  stat=05  cmd=2 (CMD_OK)   -> re-read returned 63, 65, 67, 73, ...
```

11 of 11 sabotaged reads returned exactly 4 with `CMD_OK`, the re-read returned the
true length every time, and the node received the same traffic as a second receiver on
the same channel - no bogus lengths, no receive errors - even though a quarter of its
length reads had been broken on purpose.

Worth adding, since it is the reason the status matters rather than just the value:
comparing the returned length against irq[31:16] looks like a cheap way to detect this
without the status byte, but 68 is both a common frame length and what irq[31:16] reads
when RX_DONE and CRC_ERROR are set together. On such frames that comparison fires while
the status correctly reports `CMD_DAT`. Measured as well.

**Expected behavior**

A read command either returns the reply to the command that was sent, or fails with a
status code. It should not be possible to receive the default status stream in place of
the requested data without any indication.

**Possible directions**

The chip already reports whether a reply is on its way, and the measurements above show
it discriminates in both directions. The command status field in stat1 has four values,
and `LRxxxx::SPIparseStatus()` currently only rejects two of them:

```c++
if((in & 0b00001110) == RADIOLIB_LRXXXX_STAT_1_CMD_PERR) { ... }
else if((in & 0b00001110) == RADIOLIB_LRXXXX_STAT_1_CMD_FAIL) { ... }
```

`CMD_OK` ("successfully processed") and `CMD_DAT` ("successfully processed, data is
being transmitted") are both accepted as success. On the read transaction of a get
command, `CMD_DAT` is the only correct one - and every stale reply measured reported
`CMD_OK`, while every genuine one reported `CMD_DAT`. Checking for it would catch this
without any timing change, and would cover every get command rather than just the
length.

The callback only receives the status byte, so it cannot tell a read from a write on
its own; it would need either a flag in the SPI config saying a data reply is expected,
or a separate check in the read branch of `LRxxxx::SPIcommand()`.

An alternative, or an addition, is the handshake itself: wait for BUSY to actually rise
before waiting for it to fall, bounded by a short timeout for the case where the command
has already completed by the time sampling starts.

Either way it would be good if the failure were visible to the caller, rather than
arriving as data that looks legitimate. An application can work around the length read
from the outside, by doing the two transactions itself and keeping the status byte, but
that only helps the one call it wraps - the other get commands stay exposed, and a wrong
RSSI or SNR has no signature to test against at all.

**Additional info**

 - MCU: nRF52840
 - Arduino core: Adafruit nRF52 Arduino core
 - Wireless module type: LR2021 (LR11x0 affected by the same code path)
 - Build environment: PlatformIO
 - Library version: 7.7.1, git 6d8934836678d8894e3d556550475b37dce3e2b6

items.title: New functions to support fewer missed transmissions.
items.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Not so much a problem as an improvement for Meshtastic to be better at doing CAD:
In two cases we need the receiver re-armed *without* dropping a packet already on the air: 
1) CAD with a GOTO_RX exit mode — the chip auto-enters RX to catch the packet CAD just detected;
2) re-arming the DIO interrupt after `RX_DONE` in continuous RX while a second packet is still arriving.

Every route back into RX goes through `startReceive()` → `stageMode(RX)`, which `standby()`s (SX126x/LR11x0) or clears IRQ + re-issues `setRx` (LR2021). All of these abort the in-flight reception, so LBT can't hand a detected packet to the normal RX path.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Add `PhysicalLayer::resumeReceive(startRx=false, irqFlags, irqMask)` basically remapping the RX IRQ and optionally re-issue `setRx`, with no preceding `standby()` for SX126x, LR11x0, LR2021 (CAD-exit-mode radios).

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
You could make the supporting functions public rather than private, or we could run in godmode.

**Additional context**
I have a drafted branch ready to go at https://github.com/NomDeTom/RadioLib/tree/rxResume, and a rather more verbose PR in with meshtastic so you can see the proposed implementation at work: https://github.com/meshtastic/firmware/pull/11137

Final disclosure: I leant heavily on Claude Code for this, but I believe the code matches the rest of the codebase and I've reviewed it as best I can.

items.title: LR1121 / SX128x LoRa incompatibility at SF11/12

labels.name: bug
labels.description: Something isn't working

labels.name: resolved
labels.description: Issue was resolved (e.g. bug fixed, or feature implemented)

items.body:
I have been experimenting with 2.4GHz LoRa modules using LoRa modulation (MeshCore using RadioLib 7.7.1).

During my tests I discovered SX1281 & SX1280 devices could communicate with each other but not with an LR1121, when using SF 11 or 12 and 406.25 KHz bandwidth.
If the LR1121 is set forceLDRO on for SF11 & 12, the module communicates with the SX128x modules as expected at all bandwidths.
For the SX128x compatible bandwidths (203.125, 406.25, 806.5) the current LR1121 symbol time based calculation gives only combination 203.125 / SF12 as requiring LRDO. In testing this is the only compatible SF11+ combination between the two modules currently (without use of forceLDRO).


The SX128x datasheet makes no mention of low data rate optimization. The LR1121 datasheet does not indicate this as being a requirement for compatibility. 
However, reading the LR2021 datasheet (section 9.9.1 SetLoraModulationParams, under table 9-4) I found this gem:

Recommended settings for ldro are:
* 0 for SF5-10, BW250 / SF11, BW500, BW1000
* 1 for all other BW and SF11/12 (including SX1280 compatible bandwidths BW800/400/200)

It would seem Semtech thinks this is a requirement for SX128x compatibility, at SF11/12, with the LR2021.
Unfortunately I don't have a LR2021 to test this with currently. 

The auto LDRO calculation seems common to both devices, possibly a change to accommodate SX128x compatibility would be beneficial.

items.title: Scanchannel / CAD hang
items.body:
**Describe the bug** On a Semtech LR2021, `scanChannel()` never returns on an idle channel - it hangs forever. `startChannelScan()` succeeds and the CAD runs, but the blocking wait `while(!this->mod->hal->digitalRead(this->mod->getIrq()))` never sees the IRQ pin assert. Root cause (checked on hardware): the **CadDone interrupt latches in the IRQ status register (~19 ms after the scan starts) but is never asserted on the DIO pin** when the CAD exits back to standby (the `CAD_ONLY` exit mode `scanChannel()` uses). The status register clearly shows CadDone (bit 20), the DIO IRQ mask is correct (`0x00100080` -> DIO5), and DIO5 is configured as IRQ - yet the pin never toggles, not even a 1 us pulse (microsecond-resolution poll). Rx/Tx work only because they attach a hardware edge interrupt to a pin that does assert; CAD's software poll of the pin can never complete. For context, this looks like a residual of #1727 (merged, present in 7.7.1). That PR fixed the CAD *command* path (SetLoraCadParams / SetLoraCad), so CadDone is now generated correctly - but `scanChannel()` still hangs, because its wait loop polls the DIO pin rather than the status register, and CAD completion never reaches the pin. Fix that works: poll the IRQ **status register** in `scanChannel()` (which `getChannelScanResult()` already reads) instead of the DIO pin, bounded by a timeout derived from the CAD duration. `scanChannel()` then returns `RADIOLIB_CHANNEL_FREE` in ~19 ms. Also, unrelated but spotted while here: the CAD exit-mode constants don't match datasheet Table 6-18 - `CAD_RX` should be `0x01` and `CAD_LBT` `0x10`, but RadioLib has `CAD_EXIT_MODE_TX = 0x01` / `CAD_EXIT_MODE_RX = 0x02`; `0x02` returns a command error on the chip. The default `0x00` (CAD_ONLY) path is unaffected. A two-commit fix is ready and hardware-verified if a PR is welcome.
Debug mode output

Not standard RadioLib debug output - this is my instrumented probe reading the raw IRQ status register versus the DIO pin during CAD: ``` [startScan] irqFlags=0x00000180 mapped=0x00100080 dio=5 ; CAD_DONE|CAD_DETECTED correctly mapped to DIO5 ; CAD completes: IRQ status = 0x00100000 (CAD_DONE) at ~19 ms ; DIO pin (GPIO14) tight-polled 60 ms at microsecond resolution: everHigh=0, transitions=0 ; => CadDone latches in the status register but never asserts the DIO pin (CAD_ONLY exit mode) ; after the fix (scanChannel polls the IRQ status register): scanChannel() -> -15 (RADIOLIB_CHANNEL_FREE) in 19ms ; was: hang forever ```

**To Reproduce**
Minimal sketch that hangs

```c++ #include // LR2021 wiring (Meshnology W12 / "WiFi LoRa 32 V5"); adjust pins for your board. // radio DIO5 is wired to the MCU IRQ pin, which matches radio.irqDioNum (default 5). LR2021 radio = new Module(8 /*NSS*/, 14 /*IRQ = radio DIO5*/, 12 /*RST*/, 13 /*BUSY*/); void setup() { Serial.begin(115200); SPI.begin(9 /*SCK*/, 11 /*MISO*/, 10 /*MOSI*/, 8 /*NSS*/); int state = radio.begin(906.875, 250.0, 11, 5, 0x34, 22, 8, 0.0); Serial.printf("begin=%d\n", state); // Hangs forever on an idle channel: CadDone latches in the IRQ status register // but is never asserted on the DIO pin, so the pin-poll never returns. int cad = radio.scanChannel(); Serial.printf("scanChannel=%d\n", cad); // never reached } void loop() {} ```

**Expected behavior** `scanChannel()` returns promptly with `RADIOLIB_CHANNEL_FREE` (or `RADIOLIB_LORA_DETECTED` when activity is present) instead of blocking forever. **Screenshots** N/A. **Additional info (please complete):** - MCU: ESP32-S3 - Link to Arduino core: https://github.com/espressif/arduino-esp32 (via pioarduino platform-espressif32 55.03.39) - Wireless module type: Semtech LR2021 (LR20xx family) - Arduino IDE version: PlatformIO (Arduino framework), not the Arduino IDE - Library version: `master` (git `3c960d0e4`, reports 7.7.1) Diagnosed and written with AI assistance.

items.title: FLRC mode: readData()+startReceive() per-packet overhead limits throughput on ESP32-C3

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: wontfix
labels.description: This will not be worked on

items.body:
During FLRC throughput characterization on ESP32-C3 + LR2021 (RadioLib 7.6.0), we found that the RX pipeline takes ~4ms in SPI overhead per packet, limiting achievable throughput to 80 kbps at 2600 kbps air rate (3% utilization).

Hardware: ESP32-C3 @ 80 MHz, NiceRF LoRa2021, FLRC 2600 kbps, 255-byte fixed-length packets.

Per-packet SPI breakdown (measured via esp_timer):

| Operation | SPI round-trips | Time |
|-----------|----------------|------|
| getPacketType() | 1 | ~0.2ms |
| getPacketLength() | 1 | ~0.2ms |
| readRadioRxFifo() (255B burst) | 1 | ~0.2ms |
| clearRxFifo() | 1 | ~0.2ms |
| clearIrqStatus() | 1 | ~0.2ms |
| standby() | 1 + BUSY wait | ~1ms |
| startReceive() | 1 + BUSY wait | ~1ms |
| Total | 7+ | ~4ms |

For comparison, raw SPI register access (CMD_READ_RX_FIFO + CMD_CLEAR_IRQ) achieves the same result in 2 commands / 0.4ms — a 10x reduction in SPI overhead. We measured 838.8 kbps end-to-end with 500/500 packets, 0% PER using this approach.

The core question: the radio stays in RX mode during FIFO read on the LR2021 (it has an auto-RX feature). The standby()→startReceive() cycle appears unnecessary if the caller does not need RSSI or mode transitions between packets.

Suggestion: an opt-in `readDataFast()` (or similar) that:
1. Skips getPacketType() (caller knows the modem)
2. Skips clearRxFifo() (radio auto-clears on next RX)
3. Combines IRQ read + clear
4. Optionally stays in RX mode (no standby)

This would only matter for FLRC and high-rate GFSK — LoRa users are unaffected (air time dwarfs processing overhead).

I have working raw SPI bypass code with full measurement data. Happy to contribute a PR if there is interest in this direction.

items.title: LR2021: expose detector index from GET_LORA_PACKET_STATUS

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

items.body:
The LR2021 supports multi-SF reception via side detectors configured through `setSideDetector()`. When a packet is received, the chip reports which detector (main or side 1/2/3) caught it in the response to `GET_LORA_PACKET_STATUS`. This information is currently read into `buff[5]` but only the RSSI LSBs (bits 1:0) are extracted -- the detector field in bits 5:2 is discarded.

Exposing this field would complete the multi-SF receive path: users can configure side detectors, receive packets on different spreading factors, but currently have no way to determine which detector/SF a given packet arrived on.

### Proposed change

Add an optional 7th parameter `uint8_t* detector = NULL` to `getLoRaPacketStatus()`:

**LR2021.h:**
int16_t getLoRaPacketStatus(uint8_t* cr, bool* crc, uint8_t* packetLen = NULL,
    float* snrPacket = NULL, float* rssiPacket = NULL,
    float* rssiSignalPacket = NULL, uint8_t* detector = NULL);

**LR2021_cmds_lora.cpp** (after the rssiSignalPacket block, before `return(state)`):
if(detector) { *detector = (buff[5] >> 2) & 0x0F; }

The value is a one-hot bitmask per the datasheet:
- `0x01` -- Main detector
- `0x02` -- Side detector 1
- `0x04` -- Side detector 2
- `0x08` -- Side detector 3

### Notes

- Fully backward-compatible: the new parameter defaults to `NULL`, so existing callers are unaffected.
- The data is already in `buff[5]` from the existing SPI read -- no additional chip communication needed.
- Follows the same optional-out-pointer pattern used by the other parameters in this function.
- We have already implemented this patch in our project and verified it is functional on hardware with multi-SF reception across 4 simultaneous spreading factors: https://github.com/dasmensch-su/Meshtastic-nRF54L15-LR2021-Multi-SF

This is a place holder for supporting the LR2021.
The SX127* series was the first gen chips and had 20dbm with OOK support.
The SX126* series was the second gen, got OOK support removed, the reception got better and the output power got to 22dbm
The LR1121 is the third gen of the chips and is already supported by RadioLib
The LR2021 is the forth gen that got released this week in the press release here: https://www.semtech.com/company/press/semtech-launches-lora-plus-lr2021-transceiver-with-lora-gen-4-technology

The really great improvement of the LR2021 looks to be TCXO by design and not optional any more. 
Something many people at Meshtastic would love and change the whole mesh network: Multi-spreading factors (SF) receiver
On the one hand this would improve the range by making it possible to use the slowest possible speed when you are far away walking and on the other hand you can use for example the Short Fast mode to have much higher speed and make it possible to get more people on the same frequency.

items.title: RL2021 cannot provide hasCRC and rxCR required by computePacketTime()

labels.name: enhancement
labels.description: New feature or request

labels.name: resolved
labels.description: Issue was resolved (e.g. bug fixed, or feature implemented)

items.body:
**Problem Description**
When attempting to use RL2021 supported by RadioLib in Meshtastic, I encountered an issue related to packet time calculation.
In Meshtastic, when adapting the getPacketTime() function, the implementation eventually calls:
`computePacketTime()`
Inside this function, the following API is required:
`lora.getLoRaRxHeaderInfo(&rxCR, &hasCRC);`
This function retrieves two parameters:

- rxCR (coding rate)
- hasCRC (whether CRC is enabled)

These parameters are required for correct packet time computation.
For LR1110, this works correctly because getLoRaRxHeaderInfo() is implemented in the LR11x0 driver.
However, RL2021 does not support this command, which prevents proper packet time calculation in Meshtastic.

**Root Cause**
Although RL2021 does not support the getLoRaRxHeaderInfo command, the same information (rxCR and hasCRC) can be obtained using:
`getLoRaPacketStatus`
However:
This command is not exposed through a public API in RadioLib.
The function is private, making it inaccessible from external frameworks like Meshtastic.
As a result, Meshtastic cannot retrieve the required parameters when using RL2021.

**Proposed Solution**
Possible solutions include:
Implement a method similar to getLoRaRxHeaderInfo() for RL2021, internally using the getLoRaPacketStatus command.
or
Provide a public API that exposes the information from getLoRaPacketStatus, allowing access to:
  -hasCRC
  -rxCR（coding_rate）
This would allow RL2021 to work correctly with code paths that rely on computePacketTime().

RL2021 should provide a way to retrieve hasCRC and rxCR so that computePacketTime() can function correctly in higher-level frameworks like Meshtastic.
If this approach makes sense, I would be happy to help test or contribute a patch.

items.body: With my collection of sx1280 devices finally able to be used (Thank You!), I have been enjoying the ability to do some over-the-air testing. Transmitted bytes between two devices programmed with the same code work perfectly. As a final check, I thought I would record a packet on an SDR to confirm that the received packets look "right". There's obviously a good chance that I'm doing something incorrectly, but when examining a received packet, it appears that the **invertIQ** command is producing the opposite result of my intention. In my code, the **IQINVERTED** parameter is set along with all of the other standard LoRa paramenters: `#define IQINVERTED false` ... and then when the radio is initialized, that parameter is used with the **radio.invertIQ** command as shown here (I have temporarily added a PRINT statement to confirm the value being used): So, with IQINVERTED set to 'false', the serial monitor reflects that value correctly: ... however, upon examination of the received over-the-air packet, the waveform is clearly inverted: (yes, there is a lot of noise on 2.4 GHz) As a cross-check, I set IQINVERTED to 'true' and the over-the-air result is the opposite... a packet received with the normal, non-inverted orientation. Many thanks if someone could please confirm if `radio.invertIQ` is behaving correctly for the **sx128x** devices or if I am just using it incorrectly. Thanks!
